UnitStatement: AGENTS.md maps the general Chirality agent framework onto OpenPipeStress development.
AGENTS.md does not redefine the canonical agent framework; it specifies how existing agent roles are used for this project.
Executable prompts and TASK briefs must derive paths from the active checkout.
Resolve REPO_ROOT with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
Set WORKING_ROOT to {REPO_ROOT}/projects/chirality-piping.
Use {REPO_ROOT} and {WORKING_ROOT} in project-local instructions and briefs instead of machine-specific absolute paths.
Normative agents define constraints: data boundary, solver architecture, validation, and professional responsibility.
Operative agents execute bounded deliverables: code, tests, schemas, GUI slices, docs, and reports.
Evaluative agents review, reconcile, audit, and decide whether outputs are acceptable for the next stage.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP (Type 1) maintains _Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md, scope ledger, packages, deliverables, context budget, and open issues.
PREPARATION (Type 2) scaffolds package and deliverable folders from the decomposition.
TASK (Type 2) executes one sealed deliverable using an appropriate skill/profile.
REVIEW (Type 1) reviews deliverables against scope, tests, data boundary, and acceptance criteria.
RECONCILIATION (Type 1) detects cross-package conflicts, overlaps, stale assumptions, and inconsistent terminology.
CHANGE (Type 1) performs final Git/file-state closeout for validated tranches: scoped status review, staging, commit, and fast-forward-safe push.

RESEARCH (Type 1) performs evidence-grounded, read-only inquiry over accepted decompositions, source/standards catalogs, and retrieval indexes, returning cited findings without changing project state.
AUDIT_* (Type 2) runs bounded checks for decomposition coverage, governance conformance, dependency closure, and epistemic integrity.
Use bounded app-integration or lifecycle tranches by default.
A parent WORKING_ITEMS agent may orchestrate parallel TASK fan-out only when subscopes are separable, briefs are explicit, and write scopes are disjoint.
Agents may write inside the selected tranche scope, required evidence and coordination artifacts, and project-local plans created under the issue-plan rule.
Do not write root governance files, root agent instructions, root skills, or root tools unless the human explicitly directs that governance work.
Other agents may be working in this monorepo with disjoint write scopes; treat unrelated dirty files outside the selected tranche scope as external state.
Do not fix, stage, revert, or interpret unrelated dirty files outside the selected tranche scope unless the human directs that work.
When a tranche is complete, validated, and project closeout rules allow it, the parent WORKING_ITEMS agent hands off to a CHANGE agent/subagent for final Git/file-state review.
CHANGE should commit and push the validated tranche as the ordinary terminal action when git state allows closeout.
Per-run APPROVE: tokens are not required for scoped closeout commit/push.
If a CHANGE agent/subagent is unavailable, perform the CHANGE closeout checklist inline.
CHANGE closeout: inspect root git status.
CHANGE closeout: confirm validation evidence and skipped-check notes.
CHANGE closeout: stage only files in the selected tranche write scope, required evidence/coordination artifacts, and any explicitly created governance-issue plan.
CHANGE closeout: do not stage unrelated dirty files.
CHANGE closeout: commit the scoped tranche when validation and staging are clean.
CHANGE closeout: fetch or otherwise verify upstream state before pushing.
CHANGE closeout: push only when the upstream branch can be fast-forwarded to the local scoped commit.
If the remote branch has advanced and local HEAD does not already include it, stop and surface the conflict.
Do not merge, rebase, force push, or judge another agent's work during ordinary closeout.
Git closeout is source-control hygiene; it is not lifecycle issuance, release readiness, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance acceptance.

If concrete, actionable issues that would improve the agentic development loop, project governance, agents, or skills are discovered, record them in at most one timestamped plan under {WORKING_ROOT}/plans/ for the session.
Do not create a plan merely to satisfy the issue-plan instruction when no actionable issue was found.
Project-specific TASK profile labels are proposed; they may be implemented as skills or as explicit sealed briefs.
Profile solver-core covers PKG-04 and PKG-05 solver/load/stress deliverables.
Profile domain-schema covers PKG-02, PKG-03, PKG-06 schemas and data models.
Profile rule-pack-engine covers PKG-06 evaluator and completeness-check deliverables.
Profile gui-workflow covers PKG-07 GUI deliverables.
Profile report-audit covers PKG-08 report and reproducibility deliverables.
Profile validation-qa covers PKG-09 verification/validation deliverables.
Profile interop-build covers PKG-10 API, plugin, packaging, and FEA handoff deliverables.
Profile docs-education covers PKG-11 documentation and invented-example deliverables.
Profile security-privacy covers PKG-12 private-data and telemetry deliverables.
Profile ip-governance covers PKG-01 and data-boundary deliverables.
Every Type 2 execution must receive one DeliverableID.
Every Type 2 execution must receive the parent PackageID.
Every Type 2 execution must receive scope items and objectives from _Registers/Deliverables.csv.
Every Type 2 execution must receive applicable invariants from CONTRACT.md.
Every Type 2 execution must receive acceptance criteria from _CONTEXT.md or the sealed brief.
Every Type 2 execution must receive an explicit write scope.
If a requested task crosses package boundaries or requires protected data, stop and escalate to SOFTWARE_DECOMP or the human project authority.
